newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Four Indonesians arrested over suspected explosives.
newsitem.headline: Four Indonesians arrested over suspected explosives.

text.p: The Indonesian military has arrested four men it suspected were planning to set off an explosion at a shopping mall in north Jakarta, a newspaper reported on Wednesday.

"The four are believed to belong to a group which always tries to cause trouble in the capital, with the ultimate goal of disrupting the general elections," Jakarta military commander Major-General Sutiyoso was quoted as telling the Jakarta Post newspaper.
Military officers could not be reached for comment.
The paper said officers became suspicious after the men were seen wandering around the Kelapa Gading shopping centre early on Tuesday morning.
It said the officers later confiscated stones and gasoline from the men, but did not find any bombs.
The paper gave no further details.
Indonesia has been rocked by the worst political violence in more than 30 years during an election campaign contested by three political parties. Voting takes place on Thursday.

Thousands of party supporters have taken to the streets in Jakarta and elsewhere during the campaign in what some analysts said was a spontaneous outbreak of partisanship and youthful exuberance, as well as frustration with a system which allows political demonstrations for only a month every five years.
The official Antara news agency quoted Sutiyoso as urging Jakarta voters not to hesitate to cast their ballots despite Tuesday's scare at the mall.
The agency gave no further details.
Polls open from 8 a.m. to 2 p.m. (0100-0700 GMT). Major results are expected within 24 hours.
Analysts have said the result of the poll was a foregone conclusion with the ruling Golkar party expected to win easily.
The other parties contesting the election are the Moslem-oriented United Development Party and the Christian-Nationalist Indonesian Democratic Party.
